# Build and validate a clinical ML model in R {.center}

::: {.notes}
Voce docente (IT): apertura. L'arco dell'intera giornata è `fit → tune → validate`,
sul dataset heart-failure clinical records (299 pazienti, esito: morte). Il
deliverable finale è un report Quarto riproducibile. Mentre carico/scaldo
`renv::restore()` in background, anticipo le quattro tappe: setup pulito, dati
ordinati, una spina logistica, lo zoo tunato.
:::

We will spend the afternoon doing one thing well: take a real clinical cohort
(**heart-failure clinical records**, 299 patients), and **build, tune, and validate**
a model that predicts in-hospital death — ending with a **reproducible report** a
colleague can re-run.

- The spine is **tidymodels**: `rsample` $\to$ `recipes` $\to$ `parsnip` $\to$ `workflows` $\to$ `yardstick`.
- One outcome, four algorithms, **one** honest test-set evaluation.
- Everything live-coded, everything reproducible (`renv` + `here` + `set.seed`).

# Step 00 · Setup {#sec-00-setup .center}

<!-- Step 00 (demo, 10 min): open `.Rproj`, `renv::restore`, load with `here` + `rio`. -->

**Objective.** Start from a healthy, reproducible project.

- Open the `.Rproj`; let `renv::restore()` rebuild the pinned library.
- Load data through `here::here()` (stable paths) and `{rio}::import()`.

::: {.notes}
Voce docente (IT): demo (~10 min). Ambiente sano = precondizione di tutto. `renv` è
già in restore in background dall'opening. Mostro `renv::status()` in sync e
`here::here()` che punta alla root del progetto. Live-check al minuto 9: GREEN/RED.
:::

# Step 01 · Import & wrangle {#sec-01-import .center}

<!-- Step 01 (hands-on, 32 min): tidyverse primer; clean/recode with dplyr/tidyr and `|>`; outcome to factor. -->

**Objectives.** Meet the tidyverse and shape the data.

- A tidyverse primer: the native pipe `|>`, verbs that **return a new tibble**.
- Clean and recode with `dplyr`/`tidyr`; `janitor::clean_names()`.
- **Drop the leaky `time` column** (follow-up days mechanically anticipate death).
- Make the outcome a factor with the **event first** (`died`) — so every metric
  scores death as positive by default.

::: {.notes}
Voce docente (IT): hands-on, il più lungo (~32 min) — apposta, perché è il picco di
carico-sintassi per Lucia (zero R). Rete fall-behind con la cartella `01-import/`.
"Your turn" al min 30: `clean_names → select(-time) → outcome event-first → factor
dei flag → glimpse` (12 colonne). Il drop di `time` è la mini-lezione di LEAKAGE
(giorni di follow-up anticipano la morte). MCQ al min 31 sulla semantica pipe/verbi.
:::

# Step 02 · Clinical EDA {#sec-02-eda .center}

<!-- Step 02 (hands-on, 22 min): tbl_summary(by = outcome); one ggplot; read imbalance -> metric choice. -->

**Objectives.** Describe the cohort and read its shape.

- `gtsummary::tbl_summary(by = outcome)` — a table Marco already recognises.
- One `ggplot` to see a predictor against the outcome.
- **Read the class imbalance** (~32% events) $\to$ it drives the **dual-metric** choice
  (ROC-AUC **and** PR-AUC) later.

::: {.notes}
Voce docente (IT): hands-on *elastico* (~22 min, comprimibile se siamo in ritardo).
L'imbalance ~32% qui visto in tabella è il seme del ragionamento "accuracy inganna →
guardiamo DUE metriche, ROC-AUC e PR-AUC" dello step 04. MCQ al min 50 proprio su
questo (perché due metriche, e cosa è la baseline della PR-AUC). Boxplot di
`ejection_fraction`: chi sopravvive ha frazione d'eiezione più alta.
:::

## Supervised vs unsupervised — a one-sentence bridge

Today every model **learns from a labelled outcome** (`died` / `survived`) — that is
**supervised** learning.

::: {.fragment}
**Unsupervised** learning (finding structure with *no* labels — clustering, PCA)
exists and you met the paradigm in the Overview; it is **deliberately out of scope**
here so we can do one supervised pipeline thoroughly.
:::

::: {.notes}
Voce docente (IT): una sola frase-ponte (cfr. spec §6). L'unsupervised hands-on è
tagliato di proposito (niente carico cognitivo gratuito). Resta concetto, già
incontrato nell'overview ch01. Non apriamo cluster/PCA qui.
:::

# Step 03 · Logistic spine {#sec-03-logistic .center}

<!-- Step 03 (hands-on, 38 min): object-map rsample -> recipes -> parsnip -> workflows -> yardstick; glm baseline. -->

**Objectives.** Lay the tidymodels spine with a `glm` baseline.

- Frame the task as **supervised** (one sentence on unsupervised, out of scope).
- Walk the **object-map** `rsample` $\to$ `recipes` $\to$ `parsnip` $\to$ `workflows` $\to$ `yardstick`.
- Fit a plain `glm` baseline and score it with `yardstick` — **ROC-AUC and PR-AUC**.

::: {.notes}
Voce docente (IT): hands-on (~38 min). È la zona di rischio per profondità: 7 oggetti
nuovi nell'object-map. Mitigazione: ancorare la mappa a `glm` (riconoscimento, non
nuova astrazione) e insegnarla come **una** mappa. "Your turn" min 72: `glm` vs
workflow danno la stessa AUC ("same model, more scaffolding"). Break subito dopo.
:::

## The tidymodels object-map {.smaller}

One spine, reused all afternoon. **Five objects, one chain:**

```{mermaid}
%%{init: {'flowchart': {'nodeSpacing': 24, 'rankSpacing': 32}}}%%
flowchart LR
  RS["rsample<br/>split train / test"] --> RC["recipes<br/>preprocess"]
  RC --> PS["parsnip<br/>model spec"]
  PS --> WF["workflows<br/>recipe + model"]
  WF --> YS["yardstick<br/>score (ROC-AUC + PR-AUC)"]
```

- **`rsample`** — `initial_split()` / `vfold_cv()`: who trains, who tests.
- **`recipes`** — dummy-code, drop zero-variance, normalize.
- **`parsnip`** — declare the model once, engine-agnostic.
- **`workflows`** — bundle recipe + spec so nothing leaks.
- **`yardstick`** — `roc_auc()`, `pr_auc()`: two complementary scorers.

::: {.notes}
Voce docente (IT): questa mappa è la spina dorsale riusata tutto il pomeriggio. Lo
step 04 cambia solo il nodo `parsnip` (engine-swap) e moltiplica per quattro. Tutto
il resto resta identico → "1 cosa, 4 manopole", non 4 pipeline.
:::

# Hyperparameters, one algorithm at a time {.center}

Same map, **one knob at a time.** For each algorithm: *what the knob is* $\to$ *what it
controls* $\to$ *its effect on bias / variance / overfitting.*

::: {.notes}
Voce docente (IT): le 4 slide-parametro precedono il tuning. Introducono `PARAM/BV`
un algoritmo per volta, così lo step 04 (picco di ampiezza, 10 nodi) non esplode.
Ogni slide è ~4 min. Non si tuna ancora nulla: si capiscono le manopole.
:::

## Penalized logistic — `penalty` / `mixture` {.smaller}

The `glm` baseline, **regularized**: shrink coefficients to trade a little bias for
much less variance.

| knob | what it means | effect |
|---|---|---|
| `penalty` ($\lambda$) | strength of shrinkage toward 0 | $\uparrow$ penalty $\to$ more bias, less variance (guards overfit); too high $\to$ underfit |
| `mixture` ($\alpha$) | ridge ↔ lasso dial | `0` = **ridge** (shrink all); `1` = **lasso** (some coefs $\to$ exactly 0, selects); in between = **elastic-net** |

- Regularization is the **bias–variance knob** made explicit: more penalty = simpler model.
- Engine `glmnet`; both left as `tune()` in the `workflow_set`.

::: {.notes}
Voce docente (IT): collega al glm dello step 03 — "stesso modello, con un freno".
`mixture` non tocca bias/variance da solo: sceglie *come* si penalizza (ridge vs
lasso vs elastic-net). Lasso fa anche selezione di variabili (coef esattamente 0).
:::

## k-NN — `neighbors` {.smaller}

Predict from the **`k` closest** patients. The single knob `neighbors` *is* the
bias–variance dial.

| `neighbors` (k) | behaviour | bias / variance |
|---|---|---|
| **small** k (e.g. 1–3) | follows local noise, jagged boundary | **low bias, high variance** (overfits) |
| **large** k | averages over many neighbours, smooth boundary | **high bias, low variance** (can underfit) |

- No "more is always better": k is a tradeoff, not a quality score.
- k controls flexibility only — it is **not** just a speed setting.

::: {.notes}
Voce docente (IT): qui atterra la MCQ del min 118 (direzione bias-variance del k).
Distrattori diagnostici: "più k sempre meglio", "k solo velocità", "direzione
invertita". Slide pensata per smontarli prima che emergano.
:::

## SVM (RBF) — `cost` / `rbf_sigma` {.smaller}

Separate the classes with a **margin**; the RBF kernel lets the boundary curve.

| knob | what it means | effect |
|---|---|---|
| `cost` (C) | penalty for margin violations | $\uparrow$ cost $\to$ harder margin, fits training tighter $\to$ **lower bias, higher variance** (overfit risk) |
| `rbf_sigma` ($\sigma$) | kernel **reach** (how far one point's influence extends) | large $\sigma$ $\to$ wider reach, smoother boundary (more bias); small $\sigma$ $\to$ local, wiggly (more variance) |

- The two knobs interact: a soft margin (`cost`↓) with a local kernel (`rbf_sigma`↑) are both regularizers.
- Engine `kernlab`; both `tune()`d together.

::: {.notes}
Voce docente (IT): `cost` = morbidezza del margine; `rbf_sigma` = portata del kernel.
Si tunano insieme perché interagiscono. Compatta apposta — è una slide da ~4 min.
:::

## Random forest — `mtry` / `min_n` / `trees` {.smaller}

Many decorrelated trees, **averaged**. The knobs control *how decorrelated* and *how
deep* — and one knob is **not** an overfit dial.

| knob | what it means | effect |
|---|---|---|
| `mtry` | predictors offered at each split | small `mtry` $\to$ trees more **decorrelated** $\to$ lower variance; large $\to$ trees agree more |
| `min_n` | minimum samples in a leaf | large `min_n` $\to$ shallower leaves, simpler trees (more bias, less variance) |
| `trees` | number of trees | **stability** knob: more trees = less Monte-Carlo noise — **not** an overfitting knob (more trees won't overfit) |

- Engine `ranger`; `mtry` and `min_n` are `tune()`d, `trees` is just set large enough.

::: {.notes}
Voce docente (IT): punto chiave da non sbagliare — `trees` NON è una manopola di
overfit. Aumentarli stabilizza la stima, non la fa overfittare. `mtry` è il vero
decorrelatore (l'idea che distingue RF dal bagging). `min_n` = dimensione foglia.
:::

# Step 04 · The zoo, tuned & validated {#sec-04-zoo .center}

<!-- Step 04 (hands-on, 68 min): workflow_set + workflow_map; tune over vfold_cv; rank_results; finalize; last_fit. -->

**Objectives.** Let four models compete — fairly, once.

- Bundle the four specs into **one** `workflow_set`; tune all with `workflow_map("tune_grid")`.
- Tune over **one shared** `vfold_cv(v = 5)`; `rank_results()` / `autoplot()` to compare.
- `finalize` the winner; `last_fit()` **once** on the untouched test set.

::: {.notes}
Voce docente (IT): hands-on, il CUORE (~68 min). Picco di ampiezza (10 nodi), ma lo
scaffolding dello step 03 è già automatico → non ri-conta come carico. Un solo
oggetto `folds` riusato per tutti. "Your turn" culminante al min 150 (il summative).
Predict-output al min 165: ordinare le AUC dei 4 modelli prima del reveal.
Convenzione EVENT-FIRST (`died` primo livello) → niente `event_level` nel codice.
Il toggle parallelo `plan(multisession, workers = detectCores()-1)` è OPZIONALE:
a N=299 il tuning è di ~secondi, lo dico e lo posso commentare ("così attiviamo il
parallelismo, ma non è necessario").
:::

## Two metrics — and why a single split lies {.smaller}

**Why two.** With a ~32%-event outcome, "always predict *survived*" is ~68% accurate
and clinically useless. We watch two complementary numbers:

- **ROC-AUC** — ranking of risk across all thresholds; prevalence-free, chance $= 0.5$.
- **PR-AUC** — performance on the *positive* (death) class; no-skill baseline $=$ the
  prevalence ($\approx 0.32$), so it stays honest when the event is rare.

**The tournament (cross-validated).** Four models, one shared `vfold_cv(v = 5)`:

| model | CV ROC-AUC |
|---|---|
| **Random forest** | **0.79** |
| penalized logistic | 0.74 |
| RBF-SVM | 0.73 |
| k-NN | 0.66 |

The forest wins, and the spread ($0.79 \to 0.66$) shows the *model choice* matters.
Validated once on the untouched test set: **ROC-AUC 0.87, PR-AUC 0.75, accuracy 0.77**.

::: {.fragment .callout-warning appearance="simple"}
**A single split lies.** The plain `glm` scored a flattering **0.88** on one
75-patient test split — *above* the forest's 0.87 — yet its **cross-validated**
ROC-AUC is only $\approx 0.70$. One number on a small cohort is luck;
**cross-validation is the honest comparison.**
:::

::: {.fragment .callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Aside.** ROC-AUC is **symmetric** — the positive class doesn't change it.
**PR-AUC is not**: it depends on the positive class — which is exactly why we put
`died` *first*, so both metrics score death by default.
:::

::: {.notes}
Voce docente (IT): la winner è il **random forest** (ranger), CV ROC-AUC ~0.79; sul
test ROC-AUC 0.87, PR-AUC 0.75, accuracy 0.77. Punto chiave (il "regalo" del seed):
il glm vanilla segna 0.88 su UN singolo split di ~75 pazienti ma in CV sta ~0.70 →
un singolo numero su coorte piccola è fortuna, la CV è il confronto onesto, e il
forest la vince. L'aside lega la convenzione event-first alla PR-AUC (NON simmetrica,
a differenza della ROC-AUC). Se le due callout fragment sfondano in altezza a 1080p,
spezzo la slide (tournament | single-split-lies).
:::

# Step 05 · Reproducible report {#sec-05-report .center}

<!-- Step 05 (demo, 13 min): render cached Quarto report + renv::snapshot; pre-hook to Advanced. -->

**Objectives.** Ship the deliverable, reproducibly.

- Render a **cached** Quarto report — it reloads the validated `final_fit`, never re-tunes.
- Close with `renv::snapshot()`: pinned env + `here` + `set.seed` = runnable by a peer.

::: {.notes}
Voce docente (IT): demo (~13 min). Il report NON ri-tuna: ricarica `final_fit.rds` e
`wf_rank.rds` dallo step 04 e li presenta — onesto e veloce. MCQ riproducibilità al
min 175: `renv` + `here` + `set.seed` + report cache-ato (non "basta emailare lo
script", non "basta set.seed", non "salvare il numero finale").
:::

## Next: open the model — Advanced {.center}

You built and validated a model. **Advanced opens this very model:**

- **Interpret it** — permutation VIMP and SHAP, with the logistic as a sanity anchor.
- **Go beyond** — deep learning (`torch` / `luz` / `brulee`), and `ellmer` as a typed,
  reproducible LLM-as-ETL.

The validated `final_fit` you just produced is exactly what Advanced **reloads** on
day one.

::: {.notes}
Voce docente (IT): pre-hook ad Advanced (cfr. spec §11). L'Advanced apre RICARICANDO
il workflow finalizzato di Basic e fa `predict` su una riga — niente retrain. Poi:
interpretability (VIMP/SHAP, logistic come ancora), DL spectrum, `ellmer`, capstone
`targets`. Il payoff dei pre-hook promessi nell'overview.
:::

## Further reading — go deeper in <span style="color:#E8741E;">R</span> {.inverse .smaller background-color="#1F4257"}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}

**tidymodels & the tidyverse (free, online)**

- **Kuhn & Silge.** *Tidy Modeling with R* — `tmwr.org`. The canonical book for the spine we used (`rsample` $\to$ `recipes` $\to$ `parsnip` $\to$ `workflows` $\to$ `yardstick`).
- **Wickham, Çetinkaya-Rundel, Grolemund.** *R for Data Science* (2e) — `r4ds.hadley.nz`. tidyverse foundations and the native pipe.

**Concepts behind the build (free PDF)**

- **James, Witten, Hastie, Tibshirani.** *An Introduction to Statistical Learning* (R) — the overview's theory, in R.

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}

**Reproducibility & the next step**

- **`renv`** · **`here`** · **`set.seed`** — the three pillars we leaned on all afternoon.
- **`targets`** — Will Landau's pipeline toolkit; the backbone of the **Advanced** workshop.
- **Kuhn & Johnson.** *Feature Engineering and Selection* — `bookdown.org/max/FES`. Deeper on `recipes`.

:::
::::
